title: The World Today

features.headline: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
features.facts: Naeem Abu Nahel, who had been in the post for two months, is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.
numbers: security chief in the post for two months
features.context: The strike was the day's most consequential development in Gaza, where Israel's campaign against Hamas continues and internal security appointments have turned over quickly.

features.headline: Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine
features.facts: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.
features.context: The conviction is one of the clearest court outcomes yet in the widening story of African recruitment into Russia's war in Ukraine, which Kyiv has raised repeatedly this year.

features.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
features.facts: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York: the Chinese technology giant was convicted of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and acquitted of racketeering.
features.context: The split verdict closes a long-running US prosecution of Huawei while leaving the trade-secrets conviction standing, a result both sides can present as a partial win.

around.headline: US army to detonate 68 barrels of toxic lead in Iowa on day before Thanksgiving
around.facts: Residents were warned to stay indoors amid conflicting information about how far the dust plume could travel. The US Army is set to detonate 68 barrels, five tons, of lead azide at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday morning, the day before the Thanksgiving holiday.
numbers: blast scheduled for 10am ET on Wednesday
around.context: Lead azide is a primary explosive that becomes more dangerous as it degrades, which is why the Army chose a controlled open detonation and warned residents about the dust plume.

around.headline: A blast at a hot pot eatery in Vietnam's capital Hanoi kills 6 and injures more than a dozen
around.facts: A blast at a hot pot eatery in Vietnam's capital Hanoi killed six people and injured more than a dozen others, news agencies reported from the scene.
around.context: Hot pot restaurants cook at the table over open burners, and the blast was the deadliest single incident reported from Vietnam in the day's intake.

around.headline: What to know about US Army plans to blow up a stockpile of lead azide in Iowa
around.facts: An explainer on the US Army plan to blow up a stockpile of lead azide at the Iowa ammunition plant, the safety warnings around it, and why the degraded material cannot simply be moved.
numbers: one stockpile of degraded lead azide
around.context: The explainer ran alongside the main Iowa report because officials had given conflicting accounts of how far the lead dust could travel, and residents needed one clear account.

around.headline: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times
around.facts: Published extracts from the late pontiff's diary claim one of the visions happened in the choir loft during Mass.
numbers: three visions described in the diary
one vision in the choir loft during Mass
around.context: The diary extracts were published after the late pope's death and were the day's most unusual story: a pontiff recording, in his own hand, that he believed he had seen the devil.

desk_notes.gaza_strike: Led from the first pass: a named office-holder killed, a reported toll attached, and three carriers including an independent wire. The desk debate was whether the name belongs in the headline; it does not, because the office is the news beyond Gaza and the name is in the facts.
desk_notes.zimbabwean_conviction: Held at feature 2 as the day's only court outcome with three-region reach. The desk note is the naming rule: a recruit in a pipeline is described by nationality and role, while the pipeline itself is the story being told.
desk_notes.huawei_verdict: The split verdict is the edition's test of headline honesty. Both halves print or the story does not feature; the conviction leads the wording because it is the half with consequences still to come, starting with sentencing.
desk_notes.iowa_detonation: The grid's lead and the strip's anchor number. Its panel partner, the explainer, sits two rows down in print order but directly under it in reading order, which the layout preserves by keeping both Iowa stories in the left column's line of sight.
desk_notes.hanoi_blast: The day's worst toll, carried by two wires and no photograph. The panel decision was automatic under the house rule, and the desk note is only about the cause: the edition explains the setting and names no cause, because the wires named none.
desk_notes.iowa_explainer: Exists as a separate story because two wires carried it as one. The explainer is the day's clearest example of the duplication rule: the news itself decided the report was not enough, and the page records that decision by printing both headlines.
desk_notes.pope_diary: Placed last in the grid deliberately, as the day's only story about belief. Its figure completes the strip, and the desk note is the status discipline: claims and diary says, in the headline, the label and this record, every time.
